mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2.0% indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate by more than 0.2 percentage points over three months signals strengthening labor market conditions, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE declines by >0.2pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in real personal consumption (RSAFS > 650,000 million) and housing starts (HOUST > 1,500 thousand) indicates robust consumer demand, driving corporate revenue growth and positive equity returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when RSAFS > 650000 and HOUST > 1500.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 100 (index 2017=100) indicates weakening manufacturing activity, triggering risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 100.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth above 2.0% (GDPC1 > 19,600 billion) signals robust economic expansion, supporting corporate profit growth and positive equity returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when GDPC1 > 19600.

mechanism_narrative: CPI inflation exceeding 295 (CPIAUCSL > 295) signals persistent inflationary pressure, prompting monetary tightening that reduces equity valuations and generates negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 295.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous employment growth (PAYEMS > 150,000 thousand) and unemployment decline (UNRATE < 3.6%) indicate tight labor market conditions, increasing wage pressures and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS > 150000 and UNRATE < 3.6.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate above 4.0% signals aggressive monetary tightening, reducing risk appetite and generating negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0.
